gloss: to get involved in; to try one's hand at; to lay a hand on

definitions.gloss: to get involved in; to try one's hand at
definitions.explanation: To start doing something new or to venture into an unfamiliar area.

definitions.gloss: to lay a hand on; to resort to violence
definitions.explanation: To physically strike or harm someone.

definitions.gloss: to make a move on; to make advances toward
definitions.explanation: To attempt a romantic or sexual approach toward someone.

examples.english: I tried my hand at stocks.

examples.japanese: {知|し}らない{分野|ぶんや}に{手|て}を{出|だ}すのは{危険|きけん}だ。
examples.english: It's risky to get involved in an unfamiliar field.

examples.japanese: あの{投資|とうし}に{手|て}を{出|だ}さなければよかった。
examples.english: I wish I hadn't gotten involved in that investment.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもに{手|て}を{出|だ}すな。
examples.english: Don't lay a hand on the child.

examples.japanese: {怒|おこ}っても{絶対|ぜったい}に{手|て}を{出|だ}してはいけない。
examples.english: No matter how angry you get, you must never resort to violence.

examples.japanese: あいつは{先|さき}に{手|て}を{出|だ}してきた。
examples.english: He was the one who struck first.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}に{手|て}を{出|だ}すなよ。
examples.english: Don't make a move on her.

examples.japanese: {後輩|こうはい}に{手|て}を{出|だ}したって{噂|うわさ}が{広|ひろ}まっている。
examples.english: Rumors are spreading that he made advances on a junior colleague.

examples.japanese: {教師|きょうし}が{生徒|せいと}に{手|て}を{出|だ}すなんて{許|ゆる}されない。
examples.english: It's unforgivable for a teacher to make advances on a student.

notes:
A versatile idiomatic expression with several distinct meanings depending on context. The literal meaning is "to put out one's hand," and each sense extends this image in a different direction.

USAGE:
- Sense 1 often carries a nuance of recklessness or venturing into something one shouldn't. Frequently appears with negative outcomes.
- Sense 2 specifically means physical violence. The phrase {先|さき}に{手|て}を{出|だ}す (to strike first) is very common.
- Sense 3 implies unwanted or inappropriate romantic/sexual advances.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手|て}を{出|だ}すな: don't touch / don't get involved
- {先|さき}に{手|て}を{出|だ}す: to make the first move (in a fight)
- {手|て}を{出|だ}さない{方|ほう}がいい: better not to get involved

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手|て}を{付|つ}ける: to start on; to meddle with — similar to sense 1 but often implies beginning a task or tampering
- {手|て}を{貸|か}す: to lend a hand — has a positive connotation of helping, unlike {手|て}を{出|だ}す which often implies recklessness
